scope: Generated one-gateway packet-slot workloads with four traffic families, fixed arrivals and deadline rules, and policy-independent tenant offers. Context scale traces are generated; they are not recorded packet arrivals or a causal replay of network measurements.

common_conditions.tenant_offer_rate_semantics: Individual tenant requests per second, not batches. At each fixed 5-ms offer epoch, P(batch)=min(1, lease_rate_per_s * family_request_multiplier * 5 / (1000 * batch_size)); each accepted epoch emits batch_size requests.
common_conditions.offer_trace_control: Offer generation uses its own seeded RNG and fixed epoch, preserves the synchronized/regime-shift family multiplier, and is independent of policy, gate, planner, and controller cadence. Every run exports a lease-offer trace; the runner records its content hash and actual individual offer count/rate.
common_conditions.admissibility_guard: Every adapter uses the same frozen gateway calendar, critical-demand certificate, existing bookings, command lead, and observed request fields. The guard has no access to future realized arrivals.

gar_h.description: Guarded admission and release with the common optional deadline-headroom screen.

luu_joint_adapter.source: Luu et al., IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management, 2022, DOI 10.1109/TNSM.2022.3160352
luu_joint_adapter.mapping: J-PR principle only: jointly select a feasible subset of same-epoch finite one-hop tenant bookings, using declared deadline-derived priority and the common gateway certificate.
luu_joint_adapter.common_wrapper: The adapter retains GAR-H's frozen periodic safe-maintenance controller beneath the common gateway interface; it changes the same-epoch request-set selection only. It is not a standalone Luu et al. system.
luu_joint_adapter.priority_mapping: A study-specific deterministic gateway priority is used: shorter requested window first, then lower resource-time, then arrival order. It is not claimed to reproduce Luu et al.'s priority semantics.
not_reproduced: the paper's SLA guarantee or proof

luu_sequential_adapter.source: Luu et al., IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management, 2022, DOI 10.1109/TNSM.2022.3160352
luu_sequential_adapter.mapping: S-PR principle only: process the same-epoch finite one-hop bookings sequentially in declared deadline-derived priority order, using the common gateway certificate.
luu_sequential_adapter.common_wrapper: The adapter retains GAR-H's frozen periodic safe-maintenance controller beneath the common gateway interface; it changes same-epoch request ordering only. It is not a standalone Luu et al. system.
luu_sequential_adapter.priority_mapping: A study-specific deterministic gateway priority is used: shorter requested window first, then lower resource-time, then arrival order. It is not claimed to reproduce Luu et al.'s priority semantics.
not_reproduced: the paper's SLA guarantee or proof

yu_gateway_adapter.source: Yu et al., Journal of Systems Architecture, 2025, DOI 10.1016/j.sysarc.2025.103539
yu_gateway_adapter.mapping: Yu-inspired event-driven floor reservation/reclamation pattern only: map a tenant request to one one-hop finite deadline-constrained demand; on an arrival or booking expiry, recompute the minimum legal one-gateway floor over the full BASE-to-MAXIMUM range around the fixed active booking calendar; and independently reject proposals failing the common gateway calendar guard. Unlike GAR-H, this adapter does not run a periodic guarded-release optimizer between events.
yu_gateway_adapter.event_window: The recomputation window is the remaining span of active fixed bookings (or one slot when none remain), not the common 40-ms periodic wrapper term.
not_reproduced: redistribution of bandwidth among active tenant flows (the simulator uses irrevocable per-booking quotas)
the source proof or performance guarantees

contexts.evaluation_qualification: Evaluation contexts are separate from the calibration subset used here. They may have appeared during earlier method development and are not globally untouched prospective evidence.

traffic_block.rationale: One fixed ordinary-pressure calibration setting is used for all policies. Stress settings are prespecified evaluation blocks, not selected best cases.

tuning_grid.selection_rule: A common 5-ms control/offer decision cadence, 40-ms wrapper term (the frozen simulator default), and enabled deadline-headroom gate (eta=1.0) are fixed for every policy. The tuning contexts therefore provide a safety/calibration confirmation only; they do not select policy-specific settings. All main rows use this one fixed configuration and differ only in the studied proposal/release rule layered under the same wrapper.

main_evaluation.common_wrapper: All main policies include the same enabled GAR-H deadline-headroom gate (eta=1.0) and the same independent calendar/certificate guard. The external rows compare composite one-gateway adapters under this wrapper, not standalone source methods.
main_evaluation.unit_of_inference: family x evaluation-context cluster after averaging three seed runs and, for the overall primary contrast, all six traffic blocks; n=12 paired context clusters overall and n=3 within each workload family. A per-traffic-block contrast also has n=12. Traffic settings from the same context are never treated as independent replicates.
main_evaluation.inference: Two-sided paired sign-flip permutation p-values for the three prespecified GAR-versus-adapter primary contrasts, Holm adjusted. Pointwise family-stratified paired bootstrap intervals resample the three context clusters within each fixed workload family and are descriptive. No packet, seed, or traffic-cell pseudo-replication is used.

factorial_diagnostic.purpose: Mechanism diagnostic, not tuning or a new source-method reproduction.

oracle.scope: A small finite deterministic booking fixture is exhaustively enumerated only as a correctness diagnostic for joint subset selection. It is non-deployable and not a production opportunity bound.
